newsitem.title: EL SALVADOR: Salvador's right-wing party sees victory in poll.
newsitem.headline: Salvador's right-wing party sees victory in poll.

text.p: El Salvador's ruling right-wing Arena party on Sunday ended its campaign ahead of next week's mid-term elections by predicting victory despite polls favouring the left-wing former guerrilla opposition.

Former President Alfredo Cristiani told 10,000 party faithful gathered in the capital that the National Republican Alliance (Arena) would come out ahead in the March 16 vote to elect 39 of the Salvadoran Congress' 84 seats and 262 mayorships across the small country.

"We will win these elections," Cristiani told a raucous gathering in a local gymnasium. Behind him, giant banners with the party colours hung alongside images of the party's founder, army officer Roberto D'Aubuisson, and current president Armando Calderon Sol.
Cristiani also accused his former opponents on the battlefield, the Farabundo Marti National Liberation Front (FMLN), of promoting violence in the run-up to elections in a bid to keep voters home.
"We shall not allow ourselves to be provoked, they only want to intimidate us," Cristiani said.

Three FMLN supporters have been killed and eight injured in clashes with Arena supporters in recent weeks, the FMLN has said. Arena claimed a group of its supporters was attacked last week, injuring six.
Polls show the former guerrillas, who signed a peace treaty in 1991, are slightly ahead in what will be the country's second election since the end of the 12-year civil war.
Electoral law prohibits political campaigning from Wednesday.
